title: How much rooftop PV can the IEEE 13-node feeder take before voltage binds, and which cheap measure adds the most?
lede: Stochastic PV hosting capacity of the IEEE 13-node feeder in OpenDSS on 300 random placements: median 1,015 kW at midday minimum load, voltage binds first in 75% of placements; a 2 V lower regulator set-point adds +310 kW, while inverter fixed power factor and volt-var add about nothing once the regulators respond (modelled, not a measured feeder).
summary: OpenDSS on the IEEE 13-node test feeder (3,466 kW peak): total PV is ramped from zero over 300 random placements (1–8 customer nodes, seed 1) until the first service voltage above 1.05 pu, line above its ampacity or transformer above its kVA rating, with every measure scored on the same placements. At 30 % of peak load the median placement takes 1,015 kW (10th–90th percentile 510–1,893) and voltage binds first in 224 of 300. Lowering the regulator set-point by 2 V adds the most (+310 kW median, better on 74 % of placements, worse on 10 %, at 0.007 pu less margin at peak). A fixed power factor of 0.95 changes the median by −60 kW and the IEEE 1547-2018 Category B volt-var curve by 0, because the regulators’ line-drop compensation holds the voltage up; with taps frozen they add +110 and +60 kW, and with line-drop compensation off +50 and +10. Midday EV charging adds +10 kW because the load lands on the same 500 kVA transformer. The unmodified feeder reproduces the published IEEE voltages to 0.003 pu. Limits: one small feeder, snapshots not a day, conductor ampacities and the 1547 curve points recalled and not verified, EV load a rounded estimate, utility regulator settings not known.
